newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MOST PRICES UP ON VOLATILE HUNGARY GRAIN MARKET.
newsitem.headline: MOST PRICES UP ON VOLATILE HUNGARY GRAIN MARKET.

text.p: Maize and milling wheat futures finished higher for all but one contract while barley futures continued their recent rally on a volatile Budapest Commodity Exchange grain market, traders said on Thursday.

"It's sideways trading at the moment with a volatile market that can go up-limit or down-limit at any moment," said Gabor Herczeg of LaSalle, adding, for example, that new crop milling wheat began limit-up, moved to an unchanged level then moved back up to limit-up by the end of trade.
Milling wheat ended up by between 300 and 600 forints per tonne for July, August, September and October 1997 and down 350 to 21,100 forints per tonne for December.
Maize prices ended mixed with the March falling by limit down 400 forints per tonne 17,600 and July and December rising.
Feed barley continued its recent rally after large falls earlier in the week. March, July and August allrose to 26,180, 17,560 and 18,330 forinmt soper tonne respectively.
Herczeg added that no physical users were opening positions.
"Sellers are opening positions either for hedging or speculation on a weakening market," he said.
Total turnover was a modest 1,068 contracts or 419 million forints.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
